title: Launch corridor check-ins and regional snapshots
content:
Purpose
This doc is a compact, ops-friendly pocket guide for the upcoming Launch Corridor: a targeted, multi-region release wave for the serving-runtime and routing changes. It combines brief check-ins, a lightweight calendar, and a short draft of customer-facing release notes so eng+ops can move fast without losing context.

High-level objectives
- Roll changes to routing policy + KV-cache tweak with minimal user-facing latency delta
- Validate per-region autoscale and burst policies under controlled traffic ramps
- Exercise fallbacks: model-variant downgrade and cross-region reroute

Quick calendar (local times)
- Tue 2025-03-18 09:00 PT: Preflight sync + smoke targets set (15m)
- Wed 2025-03-19 01:00 UTC: Canary lane open (0.5% global traffic), region: us-west1 + eu-west1
- Wed 2025-03-19 03:30 UTC: Canary health check and telemetry snapshot (30m)
- Thu 2025-03-20 03:30 UTC: Ramp to 5% in target regions if signals green
- Fri 2025-03-21 12:00 UTC: Regional snapshot and fallback dry-run (simulate reroute)
- Mon 2025-03-24 00:00 UTC: Full rollout window (staged 25% increments every 2h)

Preflight checklist (owner initials)
- Confirm canary capacity reserved (+20% buffer) — AK
- Gate PRs merged & migrations applied (DB/schema, routing rules) — MT
- Precomputed KV prefixes warmed for top-100 prompts — CZ
- Observability dashboards pinned and baseline saved (latency, p95, error-rate, token-cost) — NP
- Alert thresholds verified in PagerDuty runbook & slack hooks active — AK
- Security review note: KMS key rotation check — CZ

Canary / Smoke tests (run within first 30m of canary)
- 50 synthetic requests across 5 sequence lengths (1K/2K/4K tokens) — pass p95 < 220ms
- KV-cache hit-rate should not drop > 5% relative to baseline
- Batching behavior: mean batch size within expected range for traffic profile
- Model fidelity smoke: 20 prompt-response golden set, diffing eval fewer than 2 regressions
- Sidecar metrics: GPU memory stable, no OOM events

Rollout heuristics and abort conditions
- Abort and rollback immediately if: error-rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m, p95 rises > 60% and correlates to increased 500s, or KV-cache error spike > 0.5%
- Soft hold: if p95 rises 20-40% but errors unchanged, pause and investigate for 30m
- Automatic fallback: route affected region to previous model variant when OOM or mem-pressure detected

Regional responsibilities (single point per region)
- us-west1: Miguel Torres — watch latency, autoscale events, infra alarms
- eu-west1: Claire Zhang — verify compliance logs and EU routing weights
- ap-northeast1: Noah Patel — simulate burst from local traffic generator and check quota enforcement

Notes to self / open questions
- Do we want the rollback to be immediate blue-green or gradual traffic shift? (pros/cons in notes)
- Should we enable short-lived metric sampling at 1s granularity for first 20m? Cost tradeoff but helps fast detection.
- Confirm downstream caches (edge CDN) TTL interaction with KV-cache changes. Might need cache-buster header in canary.

Customer-facing release notes (short draft)
- Title: Improved regional routing and inference stability
- Summary: We're deploying a set of improvements to how requests are routed and cached across regions. This will reduce tail latency for most requests and provide faster failover in case of regional degradation.
- Impact: No action required. Short, staged rollout over next few days. We expect small, temporary increases in internal telemetry sampling during the canary.
- Rollback plan: We will automatically revert to previous routing behavior should we detect service regressions.

Post-rollout: postmortem / follow-ups
- Collect 48h telemetry dump and attach to JIRA-INF-987
- Run regression eval suite across expanded prompt set (500 prompts) and capture quality deltas
- Cost analysis: token-cost delta per-100k requests vs baseline
- Update rollout runbook with lessons and tweak abort thresholds if needed

Quick links & artifacts
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321
- Runbook anchor: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INF-launch-corridor
- Post-deploy eval: /sheets/launch-corridor-evals-2025-03 (internal)

Raw field notes (scratch)
- 03/15 AK: warmed top-10 prefixes, saw 6% gain in hit-rate on synthetic bench
- 03/16 MT: autoscale test needed more headroom; requesting +2 instances in canary pool
- TODO: Add briefing snippet for CS to send brief note to impacted customers before full rollout

If anything looks off during the window, call the rollout channel and escalate to on-call SRE. Keep the timeline conservative; prefer holding 30m extra if any uncertainty.
